description: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) between two models—NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars)—when various optimisations are applied, relative to a Whisper large baseline. The vertical axis lists the five optimisations applied: “Normalised”, “Add Spacing”, “Remove Spacing”, “Americanisms”, and “Dates”, ordered from top to bottom. The horizontal axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large”, scaled linearly from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at regular intervals. Each optimisation has two bars, one for each model, with the NESAC ft model bars consistently longer than the SESHA ft model bars, indicating a higher WER difference for the NESAC model under each condition. The approximate values for the NESAC ft model bars are: 0.00334 (“Normalised”), 0.00319 (“Add Spacing”), 0.00311 (“Remove Spacing”), 0.00299 (“Americanisms”), and 0.00257 (“Dates”). The corresponding SESHA ft model values are: 0.00323, 0.00344, 0.00306, 0.00302, and 0.00228. The bars are not sorted by value but are presented in the order listed on the vertical axis. There are no visual emphasis or annotations beyond the bar lengths and their associated numerical labels at the end of each bar.
